stem: An Agent SDK application defines a security-review subagent that should only inspect code and report findings. In testing, the subagent sometimes edits files and runs shell commands to fix what it finds. Its agent definition has a description and a prompt but no tools field. What is the most reliable fix?

options.text: Add "Never modify files or run commands" to the subagent's prompt, stated as a firm rule.
options.why: A prompt instruction guides the model but does not stop it from calling tools it still has.

options.text: Set the subagent's tools field to read-only tools such as Read, Grep and Glob.
options.why: Without a tools field the subagent inherits every available tool; an explicit allowlist removes edit and shell access entirely.

options.text: Make the subagent's description more specific so it is only delegated review tasks.
options.why: The description controls when the subagent is chosen, not which tools it can use once it runs.

options.text: Leave Edit, Write and Bash out of the main agent's allowed_tools list.
options.why: allowed_tools only pre-approves tools; unlisted tools stay available, and the main agent may legitimately need them.

explanation: Give each agent only the tools its job needs. In the Agent SDK (and Claude Code), a subagent with no tools field inherits all available tools, so a reviewer should get an explicit read-only allowlist. Prompt rules and descriptions shape behavior but do not remove capabilities.
reference: Agent SDK docs — Subagents in the SDK
